item.title: Good, I'll hate those next few years, I guess...
item.description:
I’m not an AI power-user. I’m also not an AI naysayer. I consider myself a hands-on bystander. I’m touched by AI from both its extremes, as a contributor but also as a responsible for my team’s outcomes and delivery performance.

So, maybe call me an engaged side-liner. Like a football coach presented with a new high-tech ball, I stand at the side-line, carefully eagle-eyeing it, kicking it left, right, reading about it. And then I realize, this ball is different. Different rules of physics apply to this ball. So, I start wondering if this new ball might be what wins us the championship or the end of this beautiful sport whatsoever. And while I think, all my players and all other players in the world, start kicking and testing the same ball…

item.title: Kargo? Filling the gap!
item.description:
GitOps sounds too good to be true. The idea of syncing the state of your systems and applications from a single source of truth in Git feels so natural and intuitive. GitOps offers many advantages, like having a versioned track record of your application. However, as great as this sounds, it’s only part of the picture.

In this article, I’ll take you on my journey to discover the missing piece in GitOps and explore a tool that might fill the gap: Kargo. I’ll describe how I investigated Kargo and how something initially abstract and hard to grasp turned into a tool that left me with great conclusions.

item.title: Minecraft Server on AWS ECS Fargate Spot instances controlled by Telegram Bot, powered by Pulumi IaC
item.description:
Platform Engineering is basically like Minecraft. You carefully craft the best possible solution in a world with unlimited possibilities, only for some thing to blow up and ruin your day. Then you rebuild and create something even more awesome…

And as in real world, the fun starts, once you work together with other people. Hosting an own server requires either a rather high commitment to some public hosting provider (at least if you only play from time to time, like me) or to self-host your server with all the caveats attached.
